headline: Anthropic has opened talks with New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, who asked it earlier this week to pause its planned stock market listing, Bloomberg reports.
score_reason: Follow-up to a story we carried on 16 Oct; only the headline-level fact (talks have started) is available, with nothing on what was discussed.
importance_line: It shows Anthropic engaging with a public pension overseer ahead of its planned listing, which matters to investors and to the New Yorkers whose pensions he helps oversee, but nothing is reported about what was discussed.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Reuters, that Anthropic has opened a line of communication with Mark Levine, New York City's elected comptroller and a trustee of its pension funds, after the letter he sent earlier this week. In that letter, which we carried in our 16 Oct 2026 edition from a Reuters report citing CNBC, Levine asked Anthropic to pause its planned initial public offering (a company's first sale of shares to the public) until it sets out specific audits and controls on AI safety.
notes: Reply story: Anthropic answers Levine's letter; earlier story named in the summary. Bloomberg link is the original article (blocked); read only its headline and the Reuters one-line relay. Score lowered 6 to 5 because no detail of the talks could be verified. Details of the earlier letter come from our own 16 Oct edition.
